content: 1. Delafloxacin is indicated for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible bacteria. The recommended dosage is 300 mg intravenously (IV) every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. Alternatively, 300 mg IV every 12 hours can be administered initially, followed by a switch to a 450 mg oral tablet every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. Another option is 450 mg orally every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. 2. Delafloxacin is also indicated for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by susceptible bacteria. The recommended dosage is 300 mg IV every 12 hours for 5 to 10 days. Alternatively, 300 mg IV every 12 hours can be administered initially, followed by a switch to a 450 mg oral tablet every 12 hours for 5 to 10 days. Another option is 450 mg orally every 12 hours for 5 to 10 days. 3. The safety and efficacy of delafloxacin have not been established in certain populations or conditions. 4. Both fexinidazole and delafloxacin can prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration of these drugs should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Avoid combining fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or further prolong the QT interval. 5. Delafloxacin can reduce the effects of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. Oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and their efficacy may be reduced by antibacterial agents. Complete the antibiotic regimen 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 6. Selinexor may cause neurological toxicities. Avoid combining selinexor with medications that can cause dizziness or confusion. 7. Both delafloxacin and alfuzosin can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely when these drugs are co-administered. 8. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the absorption and effectiveness of delafloxacin by cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide. 9. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations, reducing its absorption. This interaction applies to agents such as calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, magnesium chloride, magnesium gluconate, magnesium oxide, magnesium sulfate, magnesium supplements, manganese, and zinc. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 10. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decrease delafloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 11. Sucralfate decreases the absorption and effectiveness of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after sucralfate. 12. Delafloxacin increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor patients closely when these drugs are co-administered. 13. Iron-containing products, such as carbonyl iron, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, and polysaccharide iron, decrease the absorption and effectiveness of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 14. Multivitamins, including those containing calcium or vision-related supplements, decrease the absorption and effectiveness of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 15. Delafloxacin increases the toxicity of amifampridine through an unspecified mechanism. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and co-administration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 16. Fexinidazole and delafloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 17. Magnesium supplements reduce the absorption of delafloxacin by forming an insoluble complex in the intestinal tract. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 6 hours after the quinolone. 18. Manganese decreases the absorption and effectiveness of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after manganese. 19. Multivitamins decrease the absorption and effectiveness of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after multivitamins.
